description: Azure: migrate the five services that build java.net.http.HttpClient.newHttpClient() per API call onto the shared, pooled, timeout-configured AzureArmClient, so no per-call HttpClient (and its selector/worker threads) is created. Preserve exact URIs, api-versions, pagination, bearer-token auth, and 403/non-200/permission-gap handling. Independent of FEAT-001 (AWS) and FEAT-003 (GCP) — different files.
steps: Read xamops-service/src/main/java/com/xammer/cloud/service/azure/AzureArmClient.java and AzureRightsizingService.java first (and context.json) to learn the exact injection and call pattern: inject 'AzureArmClient armClient' via constructor; use armClient.get(uri, token) / armClient.getQuietly(url, token).orElse(null) / armClient.list(url, token). Token fetch may stay as clientProvider.getCredential(subscriptionId).getToken(...).block().getToken() or switch to armClient.getToken(subscriptionId); do not change scope or URIs/api-versions.

AzureDbOpsService.armGet (~line 1266): replace the local HttpClient.newHttpClient() + GET + (2xx body else null) with 'return armClient.getQuietly(url, token).orElse(null);'. Inject AzureArmClient; remove now-unused java.net.http.* imports.

AzurePerformanceService.fetchFromAdvisor (HttpClient ~line 130): replace the hand-rolled nextLink loop + HttpClient.newHttpClient() with armClient.list(baseUri, token) and iterate the returned List<JsonNode> through parseInsights logic (each node is a value[] element). Preserve the 3-way status mapping: catch AzureArmClient.AzureArmException and map 403 (message contains 'HTTP 403'/'denied access') to PERMISSION_ERROR exactly as AzureRightsizingService.fetchFromAdvisor does; any other exception -> API_ERROR; empty -> NO_DATA; non-empty -> OK. Inject AzureArmClient.

AzureAlertsService.fetchFromMonitor (HttpClient ~line 107): same migration as AzurePerformanceService — armClient.list(baseUri, token), parseAlerts over the node list, preserve 403->PERMISSION_ERROR / other->API_ERROR / empty->NO_DATA / non-empty->OK. Inject AzureArmClient.

AzureSecurityService (HttpClient ~line 160): drop the HttpClient parameter from doGet and from fetchSecureScore/fetchAlerts/fetchAssessments/fetchSecureScoreControls. Rewrite doGet to call armClient.get(uri, token): map an AzureArmException whose message indicates 403 to the existing private PermissionException (so fetchFromDefender still returns PERMISSION_ERROR); armClient.get returns empty on 404 -> return null (matches today's 404 branch). Remove the per-call HttpClient.newHttpClient() in fetchFromDefender and all httpClient arguments. Inject AzureArmClient; remove unused java.net.http.* imports.

AzureReservationService (HttpClient ~line 141): drop the HttpClient parameter from fetchLiveData and helpers fetchReservations/fetchSavingsPlans/buildRecommendations. For the two single-page GETs (api-version 2022-11-01) use armClient.get(uri, token) and keep 403->empty-list / non-200->empty-list by treating AzureArmException/empty Optional as the empty-list case with the same warn logs. For buildRecommendations (Microsoft.Consumption/reservationRecommendations) the loop has meaningful 400 (retry unfiltered) and 204 branches plus MAX_RECOMMENDATION_PAGES and setRecommendationsUnavailableReason that armClient.list does not expose — keep its own paged loop but issue each request through armClient.get(uri, token), reading status via the returned Optional / the thrown AzureArmException message, preserving every branch. If faithful preservation of the 400/204 branches through armClient.get is genuinely impossible without behavior change, apply the documented MINIMUM fix for buildRecommendations ONLY: a single reused HttpClient field built once in the constructor with a connect timeout (mirror AzureArmClient's HttpClient.newBuilder().connectTimeout(...)) instead of newHttpClient() per call, with a comment explaining why. Inject AzureArmClient regardless.
Re-scan the azure package (grep 'HttpClient.newHttpClient()') and confirm the only remaining single cached-client builders are AzureArmClient and AzureRetailPricingService (both correct).
acceptance_criteria: No java.net.http.HttpClient.newHttpClient() call remains on a per-request path in AzureDbOpsService, AzurePerformanceService, AzureAlertsService, AzureSecurityService, or AzureReservationService.

Each migrated service injects AzureArmClient and routes its ARM calls through it (or, only for AzureReservationService.buildRecommendations if unavoidable, a single constructor-built reused HttpClient with a documented reason).
URIs, api-versions, nextLink pagination, bearer-token auth, and the 403->PERMISSION_ERROR / other non-200->API_ERROR / 404->null / empty->NO_DATA mappings are preserved per service.
mvn -q -pl xamops-service -am test -Dtest='Azure*' passes with no new failures.
findings:
Migrated all five services off per-call HttpClient.newHttpClient() onto the shared AzureArmClient (injected via constructor in each). Details:

- AzureDbOpsService.armGet: now `armClient.getQuietly(url, token).orElse(null)`; removed java.net.URI + java.net.http.* imports (only used by armGet). Preserves the original 'any 2xx -> body, everything else (incl. 404/403/5xx/transport error) -> null' contract since getQuietly swallows AzureArmException and 404 to an empty Optional.

- AzurePerformanceService.fetchFromAdvisor: replaced the hand-rolled nextLink loop + newHttpClient() with `armClient.list(baseUri, token)`; parseInsights now iterates the returned List<JsonNode> (each a value[] element) instead of a raw JSON body. Status mapping preserved exactly: first-page AzureArmException whose message contains 'HTTP 401'/'HTTP 403'/'denied access' -> PERMISSION_ERROR; any other exception -> API_ERROR; empty list -> NO_DATA; non-empty -> OK. Token-fetch failure also maps to API_ERROR. Same URI and api-version (2023-01-01).

- AzureAlertsService.fetchFromMonitor: same migration via `armClient.list`; parseAlerts now takes List<JsonNode>. 403->PERMISSION_ERROR / other->API_ERROR / empty->NO_DATA / non-empty->OK preserved. URI + api-version (2019-05-05-preview) unchanged. notifyNewAlerts/email path untouched.

- AzureSecurityService: dropped the HttpClient parameter from doGet and from fetchSecureScore/fetchAlerts/fetchAssessments/fetchSecureScoreControls; removed the newHttpClient() in fetchFromDefender and all httpClient args; removed java.net.http.* imports. doGet now calls `armClient.get(uri, token)`: empty Optional (404) -> null (matches old 404 branch); AzureArmException whose message indicates HTTP 403/denied access -> the existing private PermissionException (so fetchFromDefender still returns PERMISSION_ERROR); any other AzureArmException (401/throttle/5xx/transport) -> null, matching the old 'non-200 -> null' behaviour (the old code only threw on 403; 401/5xx fell through to null). All URIs/api-versions unchanged.

- AzureReservationService: injected AzureArmClient. fetchReservations and fetchSavingsPlans (both single-page GETs, api-version 2022-11-01) now use `armClient.get(uri, token)` with 403/other-non-200/empty all mapping to the empty-list outcome and the same 'Reservation Reader' warn guidance. buildRecommendations required the DOCUMENTED MINIMUM FALLBACK: its loop depends on distinguishing HTTP 400 (retry unfiltered), 204 (stop), and other non-200 (report exact reason via describeRecommendationFailure) plus MAX_RECOMMENDATION_PAGES/truncation, none of which armClient.get exposes (it collapses non-401/403/404/429/5xx statuses to an empty Optional, making 400 indistinguishable from 204). So buildRecommendations keeps its own paged loop but issues requests through a single reused `recommendationsHttpClient` field built once in the constructor with HttpClient.newBuilder().connectTimeout(10s).followRedirects(NORMAL) (mirrors AzureArmClient) instead of newHttpClient() per call. A field javadoc explains why. No status/branch behaviour changed.

Verification: `mvn -pl xamops-service -am compile` OK; `mvn -pl xamops-service -am test -Dtest='Azure*' -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false` -> Tests run: 94, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0, BUILD SUCCESS (the -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false flag is required because -am pulls in permissions-common, which has no Azure* tests). grep 'HttpClient.newHttpClient()' in the azure package: no live calls remain (only two matches, both inside Javadoc/comments in AzureCostQueryService and AzureArmClient describing the old pattern). Remaining 'HttpClient.newBuilder()' single cached-client builders: AzureArmClient, AzureRetailPricingService (both pre-existing and correct) and now AzureReservationService (documented minimum fallback).
